name: Goal Adjustment Scale (GAS)
construct: Goal disengagement and goal reengagement capacities
rights: Research/teaching use supported by co-author Michael F. Scheier's published permission for scales he helped develop; attribution required. For uses beyond research/teaching, contact the copyright holder.
source: Wrosch C, Scheier MF, Miller GE, Schulz R, Carver CS. Adaptive self-regulation of unattainable goals: goal disengagement, goal reengagement, and subjective well-being. Pers Soc Psychol Bull. 2003;29:1494-1508.

items.text: It’s easy for me to reduce my effort towards the goal.
I convince myself that I have other meaningful goals to pursue.
I stay committed to the goal for a long time; I can’t let it go.
I start working on other new goals.
I think about other new goals to pursue.
I find it difficult to stop trying to achieve the goal.
It’s easy for me to stop thinking about the goal and let it go.
I tell myself that I have a number of other new goals to draw upon.
I put effort toward other meaningful goals.

goal_disengagement.method: Reverse items 3 and 6 (1↔5, 2↔4, 3 unchanged), then compute mean or sum consistently.

safety_note: GAS scores describe goal-adjustment tendencies and are not diagnostic or suicide-risk classifications.
